primary_claim: Llama-3-8B has many redundant attention heads for an in-context-learning task: ablating heads at one layer causes backup heads at a nearby layer to take over, so the model still reaches the correct answer.
contradicts_or_qualifies: weakly supports (does not strongly confirm) Anthropic's hypothesis that in-context learning is driven primarily by induction heads
limitations_stated: This is a weaker claim than the first, and I have less evidence to support it
this is also the claim that I'm least confident about (MLPs breaking the task into subtasks)
quote: There are clearly a large number of portions of the model responsible for in-context learning.
